statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-50162 (GHSA-8xwf-rjm4-xvhv, GO-2026-5879): the oras-go file store (package oras.land/oras-go/v2/content/file) checked that a blob's title stays inside its working directory with a lexical path check that did not resolve symbolic links, so a crafted title could follow a symlink and write a file outside the working directory. It affects oras.land/oras-go/v2 before 2.6.1, in the file store's New and Store.Add (resolveWritePath). Sources: https://github.com/oras-project/oras-go/security/advisories/GHSA-8xwf-rjm4-xvhv, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5879, the fix commit https://github.com/oras-project/oras-go/commit/cc323e564d90c6b5b4bdd71d3c8d2ee2713b37e5 and https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-50162. We checked every scout-sbom-indexer-dev package published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository as of 27 November 2026: 25 builds, 1.20.4-r1 to the current 1.30.0-r0, on x86_64 and aarch64 (50 packages). Each package holds one file, /sbom-indexer, a statically linked Go program for Linux (GOOS=linux) built with CGO_ENABLED=0 (no program interpreter and no shared-library dependencies). We matched the program in every package, by the checksum the package records for it, to a copy we read in full. The -dev program is built from the same Go release and module versions as the scout-sbom-indexer program of the same version, but without the -w linker flag and without -trimpath. Its Go build information, the same on both architectures, gives the Go toolchain go1.26.2 in 1.20.4-r1, go1.26.3 in 1.20.4-r2 to 1.21.0-r0, go1.26.4 in 1.21.0-r1 to 1.21.0-r2, go1.26.5 in 1.21.0-r3 to 1.23.1-r1, go1.26.6 in 1.23.1-r3, go1.26.7 in 1.23.1-r4 to 1.23.1-r5, go1.26.8 in 1.23.1-r6, go1.27.1 in 1.23.1-r8 to 1.23.1-r10, go1.27.2 in 1.26.0-r1, go1.27.3 in 1.26.0-r2 to 1.29.0-r1, go1.27.4 in 1.30.0-r0, and oras.land/oras-go/v2, with no replacement, v2.6.0 in 1.20.4-r1 to 1.23.1-r0, v2.6.2 in 1.23.1-r1 to 1.30.0-r0. The program uses oras-go's registry client, but not its file store: in every build the function table has no function or type from oras.land/oras-go/v2/content/file, the byte string oras-go/v2/content/file does not occur anywhere in the program, and the source file table lists no file under the module's content/file directory, while the same searches find oras.land/oras-go/v2/registry/remote/auth (including (*Client).Do) and runtime.main in every build as controls. The vulnerable resolveWritePath, New and Store.Add are therefore not compiled into any build. Debian has not fixed this CVE in its trixie golang-oras-oras-go package (no-dsa, minor issue); this decision rests on the absence shown above, not on that rating.

CVE-2026-50162 (GO-2026-5879, GHSA-8xwf-rjm4-xvhv): the oras-go file content store, package oras.land/oras-go/v2/content/file, confines writes to its working directory with a lexical path check only, so a pushed blob whose title passes through a symlink inside the working directory can be written outside it. It is fixed in oras-go 2.6.1. The Go vulnerability database lists file.New and Store.Add as the affected symbols, and the fix commit adds a symlink check to (*Store).resolveWritePath in content/file/file.go. Sources: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5879, https://github.com/oras-project/oras-go/security/advisories/GHSA-8xwf-rjm4-xvhv, https://github.com/oras-project/oras-go/commit/cc323e564d90c6b5b4bdd71d3c8d2ee2713b37e5 . We checked every published trivy-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 38 builds, 0.69.1-r0 to the current 0.74.0-r12, each for x86_64 and aarch64, each verified against the repository index checksum. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/trivy, a statically linked Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0. We read its Go build information (go version -m) and its function table (go tool nm), and searched its raw bytes, which also finds the names of inlined functions. The Go build information lists oras.land/oras-go/v2 2.6.0 in builds before 0.71.2-r1, inside the affected range, 2.6.1 in 0.71.2-r1 and 0.71.2-r2, and 2.6.2 from 0.71.2-r3 on. trivy links other oras-go packages, such as the registry/remote client and its auth and credentials packages, but in every build the function table has no function of package oras.land/oras-go/v2/content/file, so neither file.New, (*Store).Add, (*Store).Push, (*Store).pushFile nor (*Store).resolveWritePath is present, while runtime.main is. The raw-byte search of every build finds no oras-go content/file name or source path, and no resolveWritePath, (*Store).pushFile, (*Store).Add or content/file.New string. As a positive control, the same function-table and byte searches on a program built against oras-go 2.6.0 that calls file.New, (*Store).Add and (*Store).Push find (*Store).Add, (*Store).Push, (*Store).pushFile and (*Store).resolveWritePath, and file.New when built without inlining. The control programs were built with Go 1.27.1, CGO_ENABLED=0, for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. The vulnerable code is not in the shipped binary.
